_comment: claudemon shield configuration. Countermeasures are OFF by default. Read the safety section of the README before arming.
_mode: off = no actions and no evaluation. monitor = evaluate and log what WOULD happen, take nothing (dry run). armed = actually execute configured actions.

auto._enabled: Automatic response to rule findings. Manual operator actions from the UI work regardless of this setting.
auto._precedence: byRule beats byCategory beats bySeverity. Actions: alert | freeze | kill | sinkhole | none.

safety._protectSessionProcess: Never signal the claude process that owns a session. Freezing it hangs the user's session; killing it ends their work. Leave true.
safety._protectPatterns: Never signal a process whose command matches any of these.
safety._requireInTree: Only ever signal processes inside the tracked Claude process tree. Leave true — this is the main guard against hitting an unrelated process.
safety._maxActionsPerMinute: Circuit breaker. Exceeding this disarms the shield back to monitor mode rather than continuing to act.
safety._autoResumeAfterS: Automatically SIGCONT a frozen process after this many seconds. 0 = stay frozen until an operator resumes it.
safety._killGraceS: SIGTERM, wait this long, then SIGKILL.

preExecution._enabled: Pre-execution gate. Requires the PreToolUse hook: python3 install-hooks.py --apply. Off means tool calls are never gated.
preExecution._mode: Caps the strongest verdict the gate may return. off = never gate. warn = record only, never interrupt. ask = escalate to the human's permission prompt. block = refuse the call outright.
preExecution._minSeverity: Floor for the generic bySeverity path only. An explicit byRule or byCategory entry is a deliberate policy statement and applies even below this floor.
preExecution._precedence: byRule beats byCategory (both ignore minSeverity), then bySeverity subject to minSeverity, then capped by mode.
preExecution._allowRules: Rule ids that must never gate a call, however severe. Use this when a rule is noisy for your workflow rather than turning the gate off.
preExecution._allowTools: Tools that are never gated. Read-only tools by default — gating them costs latency on every call for little benefit.
preExecution._timeoutMs: How long the hook waits for a verdict before applying failMode.
preExecution._failMode: open = allow the call if the monitor is down, slow or erroring. closed = deny it. Open is the default: a monitoring tool must not wedge the agent when it is not running. Choose closed only if you would rather stop than proceed unobserved.

sinkhole._neverBlock: Superseded by egress.never, which is consulted first. Kept for compatibility.
sinkhole._enforcement: What to do when a blocked host is contacted again. freeze-owner | kill-owner | none. Process-level only — see writeFirewallRules for packet-level.
sinkhole._writeFirewallRules: Generate pfctl and /etc/hosts snippets under data/ for you to review and apply with sudo. claudemon never runs sudo itself.
sinkhole._applyCommand: Optional shell template to apply a block, e.g. 'sudo pfctl -t claudemon_block -T add {ip}'. Requires a NOPASSWD sudoers entry you create yourself. Left null, nothing privileged is ever run.

audit._logFile: Every action, attempted or refused, is appended here under the data directory.

egress._comment: Outbound network policy. One authoritative list; precedence is never > block > allow > mode default.
egress._mode: monitor = classify and record, enforce nothing (default). blocklist = deny what is listed, allow the rest. allowlist = allow only what is listed, deny the rest (default-deny).
egress._never: Can never be blocked, whatever the mode or lists say. Keeps the agent's own model API and loopback reachable — an allowlist typo would otherwise strand it mid-task.
egress._block: Explicit deny. Beats any allow entry, so a broad allow cannot silently re-permit these.
egress._onViolation: alert = record only. freeze-owner = SIGSTOP the process that opened it. kill-owner = terminate it. Process-level: packet filtering needs root, so pfctl rules are generated for you instead.
egress._logAllowed: Record allowed connections too, not just violations. Verbose but useful when first building an allowlist.
